result.topic_en: Integral representations of 1 minus Euler's constant involving lacunary power series, followed by a generalisation of the Frullani-type integral giving log(1 + bc/a).
result.transcription:
we have
(7) $1-\gamma = \int_0^1 \frac{x^2+x^4+x^8+x^{16}+\cdots}{1+x}\,dx$, \quad a=b=2, c=1
(8) $1-\gamma = \int_0^1 \left(\frac{1+2x}{1+x+x^2}\right)(x^3+x^9+x^{27}+x^{81}+\cdots)\,dx$, \quad a=b=3, c=1
(9) $1-\gamma = \int_0^1 \frac{1+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{x}}{(1+\sqrt{x})(1+\sqrt{x}+x)}\left\{x^{1\frac{1}{2}} + x^{(1\frac{1}{2})^2} + x^{(1\frac{1}{2})^3}+\cdots\right\}dx$, \quad a=b=1\frac{1}{2}, c=1
and so on.
2. Similarly from the equation
(10) $\int_0^1 \frac{x^{p-1}-x^{q-1}}{\log x}\,dx = \log\frac{q}{p}$
which is true when p and q are positive, we can deduce that
(11) $\int_0^1 \frac{x^{c-1}-x^{bc-1}}{\log x}(x^a+x^{ab}+x^{ab^2}+x^{ab^3}+\cdots)\,dx = \log\left(1+\frac{bc}{a}\right)$
provided that $b>1$ and $a+c$ and $a+bc$ are positive.
3.

Integral representation of 1 - Euler's constant with a lacunary series in powers x^{3^n} (case a=b=3, c=1)

Frullani-type integral: integral of (x^{p-1}-x^{q-1})/log x over [0,1] equals log(q/p)
Generalisation with a lacunary series x^{ab^n} giving log(1+bc/a)
